propositions: MCP clients receive opaque transport timeout (-32001) after 60s while the server continues executing long gate operations (15-20 min LLM passes) and eventually signs a durable verdict that the client never observes, leaving the ticket in unknown state.

Re-invocation of review_plan/verify_completion while an in-flight run exists for the same ticket+basis launches a second billable LLM review instead of attaching to the existing run, causing paid-API cost amplification.
The MCP-only execution path (no local checkout access) lacks a durable in-progress signal or job handle, so agents cannot poll for completion or distinguish running from failed.

A singleflight in-process registry keyed on (gate_type, ticket_id, basis_ref, variant, readonly) deduplicates concurrent calls for the same gate, causing the second caller to await the first's verdict instead of launching a duplicate LLM pass.

Async start tools (review_plan_start, verify_completion_start) return a {job_id, status:'running'} handle in <100ms on a background daemon thread, with durable state persisted to the git-backed event log and polled via status tools that report six distinct states: running, passed, failed, stale-running, attaching, unknown.
The poll-status contract must document the non-terminal 'attaching' state (follower call in flight before leader's index write) to prevent agents from mis-treating it as a terminal or missing result.
